post.title: One signature turns a $1,000 stereo into $6
post.ig:
One signature can turn a $1,000 stereo into $6.

Local moves are usually billed by the hour (crew x hours); interstate moves are priced by weight and distance, plus extras like stairs, long carries, shuttles and packing.
Under FMCSA rules, a non-binding interstate estimate means the mover can't demand more than 110% of the estimate at delivery; any balance can't be demanded until at least 30 days after delivery.
Released value coverage is free but only applies if you choose it in writing; it pays 60 cents per pound per article. FMCSA's example is a 10-lb, $1,000 stereo paying $6.
Full Value Protection is the default and costs more: the mover repairs, replaces or pays current value.

Sources: FMCSA Protect Your Move, 49 CFR Part 375, This Old House (2025).
